source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Portland – Hillsboro 4 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a typical enterprise average, the same power supports roughly 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is an illustrative range, not an operator claim. The floor plate is large enough that the binding constraint on AI workloads is almost certainly power density per rack rather than raw square footage.

The certification stack qualifies the campus for a wide range of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ITAR qualifies it for defense and export-controlled technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. SSAE 18 is the audit standard underlying the SOC reports. Which tenants actually occupy the facility is not published.

Among the 133 data center facilities mapped in Oregon, only six have published a megawatt figure on their operator pages, and those six together account for 182 MW of published IT capacity in the state. This campus, at 36 MW, ranks first among those six, representing roughly 20 percent of all published Oregon capacity this site has read. That figure reflects the limits of what operators have disclosed, not a census of Oregon's total installed power.
